en: Taal Volcano features a unique nested structure with an island inside a lake inside another volcano.
Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an eight-kilometer navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The Philippine eagle, found in Mindanao forests, is one of the largest and rarest eagles in the world.
Bohol’s Chocolate Hills consist of exactly one thousand two hundred sixty-eight symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown in summer.
The Philippines sits inside the Coral Triangle, the global center of marine biodiversity with the highest number of coral species.
Baguio City is called the Summer Capital because its high elevation keeps its average temperature much cooler than Manila.
The Philippines possesses some of the world’s largest copper and gold deposits and is a top global nickel producer.
Advanced mapping technology recently updated the official count of Philippine islands from seven thousand one hundred seven to seven thousand six hundred forty-one.
The Banaue Rice Terraces were carved into the mountains of Ifugao over two thousand years ago using purely manual tools.
Mount Mayon in Albay is globally famous for its nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape formed by repeated volcanic eruptions.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching over five hundred kilometers through the Cagayan Valley.
The Philippine Sea contains the Philippine Trench, which plunges to a depth of over ten thousand meters.
